public_rationale: On August 7, 2025, OpenAI reported 89% accuracy for GPT-5 on BrowseComp Long Context inputs of 128K–256K tokens [e1]. ORCFLO's May 10, 2026 benchmark reported an Output Consistency score of 96.0 for repeated runs [e2]. Neither result measures whether users can predict individual successes and failures before seeing GPT-5's answers [e1, e2]. These results therefore do not settle the forecast about difficulty anticipating whether GPT-5 will satisfy a request [e1, e2].
limitations: The accuracy result does not show whether users could identify likely failures in advance [e1].
ORCFLO's reported consistency score does not establish users' ability to anticipate whether an answer will satisfy their request [e2].

statement.document_title: What to Expect When You’re Expecting … GPT-5

from_speaker: It will often do what you want, sometimes not
it will remain difficult to anticipate which in advance
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that users will have difficulty predicting, before seeing an answer, whether GPT-5 will satisfy their request.
The claim concerns the GPT-5 release discussed in the post. Results for later GPT-5.x models do not automatically settle it.
Mixed success rates establish that failures occur, but do not by themselves establish that those failures are difficult to anticipate.
Marcus supplies neither a numerical threshold for difficulty nor a task distribution. Representative evaluations of advance predictions would be more informative than isolated failures.
criteria.support_condition: Evaluations of released GPT-5 show that users or practical advance indicators have substantial difficulty distinguishing requests it will satisfy from requests it will fail, across a reasonably representative range of tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evaluations show that users can reliably distinguish likely successes from failures in advance across a reasonably representative range of requests, with uncertainty communicated accurately enough to guide use.

evidence.locator: Tool calling section, BrowseComp Long Context paragraph
evidence.explanation: The reported benchmark contains both successes and failures. It does not test whether users could identify those failures beforehand, so it cannot settle the central forecast.

This benchmark reports strong repeatability, which weighs against an unrestricted claim of unpredictable behavior. Its consistency score is not a measured rate of users correctly anticipating success, and its 40 English text-only cases exclude several major task types.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A reproducible evaluation comparing advance predictions by users or practical indicators with original GPT-5's actual outcomes across representative requests. It should specify model settings and success criteria, use repeated trials, and report uncertainty.
